illustrations.position_quote: More greenhouse gases slow energy loss to space, so the surface and lower air warm.
illustrations.description: Earth with sunlight arrows in labeled Shortwave and surface arrows out labeled Infrared; some infrared absorbed by gas layer and sent back down toward the surface.
illustrations.why: Shows the main process of the greenhouse effect, which text alone makes hard to picture.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Seasonal differences in land and ocean heating help cause this change.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Monsoon section now explains land-ocean heating, pressure difference and the winter-summer reversal.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Condensation releases heat, which helps keep air warm and rising.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Cyclone formation from warm water, low pressure, convection, condensation heat and rotation is taught.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Warming seawater expands and takes up more space.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Core Concept now has cause chains, social effects, government choices, mitigation and adaptation.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Land heats and cools faster than the sea.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Sea and land breezes, ITCZ, and hazards with protection each have their own subsections.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: A PAGASA bulletin reports maximum sustained winds of $130$ km/h near a cyclone's center.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Example #9 applies the typhoon band and separates it from Habagat.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: 1. Nearly all ordinary weather occurs in the troposphere. The balloon has risen above it.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Example #2 and all other solutions now use numbered steps with clue-by-clue reasoning.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Seasonal differences in land and ocean heating help cause this change.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Explains heating, pressure difference and the resulting wind reversal for both monsoons.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Moist air rises through convection, and surface air moves toward the lower-pressure center.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: Formation and sustaining of the cyclone is explained, with the role of warm water and condensation.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Its gas particles move very fast, so its measured temperature is high.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: 'Kinetic temperatures' is gone and the explanation now uses plain words.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Its usual start is from late May to early June, and it commonly ends in October.
lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.note: The dense onset and termination sentence is split into short plain sentences.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: "Classify" means put something in the correct group.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Temperature generally rises with height in the stratosphere.

lesson-earth-science-astronomy-weather-a.quote: Most meteors burn up here as they pass through the air.

science-earth-science-astronomy#75.quote: Melting glaciers and ice sheets on land add water to the sea.
